prerequisites: It is recommended to have successfully completed and understood the Fluid Mechanics course.

learning_outcomes.text: Applied knowledge of the fundamentals of fluid-mechanical systems and machines.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling students to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, abilities, and skills in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Understands the operation and applications of fluid machines.
Is capable of sizing a fluid machine subject to general technical specifications.
Has the ability to size a fluid installation.
Applies efficiency criteria in the design of an installation.
Knows how to design operation and exploitation protocols for installations based on efficiency, economy, and reliability criteria.

syllabus_topics: Introduction. Types and operation of fluid machines. Classification of fluid machines.
Review of principles. Energy exchange in turbomachines. Powers, losses, and efficiencies.
Fundamental theory of turbomachines. Geometric and kinematic aspects of flow in impellers.
1-D theory of radial turbomachines. Characteristic curves. Aerodynamic theory of axial machines and aeroturbines.
Theory of similarity in turbomachines. Modeling. Scale effects.
Operation of pumping and ventilation lines. Fluid distribution networks.
Flow regulation in pumping and ventilation lines.
Cavitation. Effects of cavitation in turbomachines. Similarity in cavitation.

assessment_methods.method: Laboratory practice questions (from global written exam)

assessment_rules: Assessment is via a global written exam composed of four parts: Problem 1, Problem 2, Theory, and Laboratory Practice Questions. A minimum of 3 out of 10 points is required in each part to be eligible for averaging. Practice attendance may influence the minimum score of each part according to criteria agreed upon at the beginning of the course. Students have the option to complete an assignment, in which case the global exam will account for 95% of the final grade and the assignment for the remaining 5%. Students must be able to demonstrate authorship of assignments and practice reports in an oral interview, failing which a grade of 0 will be assigned for those works.
